title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 3: grant analogy-order; God can destine the crown from mere grace first
pass_a_gloss: Solution. We grant that postulate, namely, that there is not any order of priority and posteriority in the acts either of the divine will or of the divine mind; but that this order is taken from analogy to the human will; and from the dependence of objects which they have among themselves. But to the comparison brought in we answer, First, that we can bring a manifest cause why an earthly prince does not designate someone singularly to the prize except from a preceding intuition of Victory, and yet God on the contrary can first from mere grace destine someone singularly to the crown, and consequently prepare and give him those gifts through which he will be foreseen as one to be brought forth to the crown.
pass_b_english: Sol. We grant the postulate: there is no priority/posteriority in the acts of the divine will or mind themselves; that order is borrowed from analogy to human willing and from how the objects depend on one another. To the comparison itself: first, we can show why an earthly prince does not mark someone out for the prize except after seeing the victory — and yet God, on the contrary, can first from mere grace destine someone singularly to the crown, and then prepare and give the gifts through which that person will be foreseen as brought to the crown.
source_text: Sol. Concedimus illud postulatum, nimirum, Non esse aliquem ordinem prioritatis & posterioritatis in actibus sive voluntatis sive mentis Divinae; sed hunc ordinem desumi ex analogia ad voluntatem humanam; & ex dependentia obiectorum, quam habent inter se. Ad inductam autem comparationem respondemus, Primo, posse nos manifestam causam afferre cur Princeps terrestris non designat aliquem singulariter ad premium, nisi ex precedente intuitu Victoriae, & Deus tamen possit e contra primo ex mera gratia destinare aliquem singulariter ad coronam, & consequenter praeparate & dare illi ea dona, per quae praevidebitur producendus ad coronam.
